# Fin connection preview

## Current ENG-13763 scope

This slice verifies which authenticated user and workspace a Fin conversation belongs to. It targets `codex/fin-foreman-preview` with the matching Acquisity app changes in [PR 6391](https://github.com/Acquisity/Acquisity/pull/6391). The internal audience remains `Foreman Preview - Aaron` on Web. On 2026-09-14, runtime `918c6d50` passed the live identity checks below on deployment `dpl_8PV8JtaPw5JXAUoxsTyEnPY1FNz9`, with Acquisity app `4199f4ff`. Local validation passed 824 tests, build and the 31-callback built GitHub proof. Both PRs remain unmerged.

The model can answer from the verified workspace name and current owner/admin role. Product investigations, diagnostic provider reads, ticket creation and delegation are not enabled in this slice. `agent/lib/fin-context-model.ts` removes tools, sets tool choice to none, and rejects generated or streamed tool calls before dispatch. `agent/agent.ts` selects that middleware for both the verified `foreman:fin-context-preview` identity and the synthetic connection probe's `foreman:fin-preview` identity. This restriction is enforced in code, in addition to the prompt.

## Identity and result contract

1. The authenticated main Acquisity app supplies a short-lived signed identity through Messenger's `auth_tokens.foreman_identity`. Start and result connectors send it as the bearer token and supply Intercom's native conversation ID as `conversation_id`. Neither value is collected or copied by Fin. The token identifies the user and live app session, not the workspace; Acquisity keeps its signing key.
2. Before starting or retrieving a result, Foreman reads that exact conversation and its sole contact through the existing Executor Intercom connection. It requires the source author to match the contact, the contact's Intercom workspace to be `ls8uffkp`, and the source URL to match the configured Acquisity origin and `/dashboard/<workspace-slug>` path. Conversation text and mutable profile workspace attributes cannot select scope.
3. Foreman passes the source slug and bearer token to Acquisity's `POST /api/internal/foreman/context`. Acquisity resolves the active workspace, verifies the token and live session, and checks actual current owner/admin membership in the main app. Expired or revoked sessions, impersonation, active bans, removed membership and other partners fail closed. Platform admin status alone grants no access.
4. Foreman checks that the returned user matches the native contact's `external_id` and the returned slug matches the source URL. It records the verified user, workspace and conversation in server-authored session context. A message asking to switch workspace does not change that context.

Every manual result lookup repeats this verification. The signed `run_handle` must match the current verified user, workspace and conversation before Foreman attaches to the saved run. Possessing an old handle alone grants no access, and handles from the earlier experiment are incompatible. An expired app token requires a refreshed authenticated app session; a valid session belonging to the same user is acceptable.

The Acquisity endpoint also accepts an explicit workspace UUID, but this Foreman intake uses only the native conversation source slug. Its response contains canonical workspace ID, slug, name, role and verified user identity. This establishes intake context; it does not grant tools permission to read arbitrary customer records.

## Preview configuration and delivery

`POST /internal/fin-preview` remains available only with `VERCEL_ENV=preview`, `FIN_FOREMAN_PREVIEW_ENABLED=true` and `FIN_FOREMAN_PREVIEW_TOKEN` configured. Normal starts and results now authenticate with the app token. The Preview secret signs result handles and still authenticates the empty-body synthetic connection probe.

Set branch-scoped `ACQUISITY_FIN_ORIGIN` to the exact HTTPS origin of the matching Acquisity Preview deployment, with no path, query or credentials. Foreman uses this server configuration both to validate the native source URL and to choose the context endpoint; neither the request nor the model may choose an endpoint. Identity verification has a 50-second bound and rejects redirects. Its two fixed Intercom reads explicitly use `foreman-fin-preview` through the existing Executor connector. Ordinary Slack and other company-service calls retain the default `foreman` toolkit; the Preview flag does not switch their toolkit. Scheduled support keeps its explicit support toolkit. Verify the Fin toolkit's live operation grants before testing. The model has no diagnostic tools even if older toolkit read grants remain installed.

Published start connector `532961` and result connector `532990` use the app-token bearer and native `conversation.id` mapped to `conversation_id`. Keep fixed `action: "start"` with `question`, and fixed `action: "result"` with `handle` read directly from the conversation attribute `Foreman Preview Run Handle`. Map each successful start's returned `run_handle` to that attribute. Result checks never start another task. Each accepted start still creates a separate task; request retries are not deduplicated.

Procedure `2124573`, `Foreman Investigation — Aaron Preview`, owns the start connector and passes its generated `foreman_report` callback URL as `callback_url`. Retain the existing one-hour webhook wait. The earlier ten-minute Procedure timeout is obsolete. That wait is distinct from the endpoint's short response observation window and the app token's expiry; this slice adds no investigation-deadline behavior.

The published Procedure trigger covers normal workspace identity and access questions and preserves the unavailable-record limitation. Output must use actual `@Read attribute` chips for `Webhook.foreman_report.message` and `Webhook.foreman_report.status`. Missing values must produce a retrieval failure. Fin acknowledges on entry; the Procedure no longer adds an acknowledgement after the connector returns. Preserve the actual answer's facts and limitations without naming internal agents. The current identity response must not be presented as a completed product investigation.

Keep `FIN_FOREMAN_PREVIEW_SLACK_CHANNEL=C0BUF4GU8C8` and the verified Preview Slack connector targeting this branch at `/eve/v1/slack`. The initial receipt and callback are stored in native channel state. Terminal events update that receipt and deliver the callback independently of the 120-second HTTP observer. Delivery is best effort with bounded requests and no retry worker; manual reauthenticated retrieval remains available. Keep both scheduled support flags false. Production routing is outside this Preview change.

## Live identity checks, 2026-09-14

- Diamond conversation `215475934884836` asked "Which workspace are you looking at?" Fin automatically answered Diamond, matching [the Slack result](https://acquisityworkspace.slack.com/archives/C0BUF4GU8C8/p1789410512630389).
- In the concurrent Demo tab, conversation `215475934933664` asked which workspace the chat was using and whether the user was an admin. Fin returned Demo and admin, matching [Slack](https://acquisityworkspace.slack.com/archives/C0BUF4GU8C8/p1789410679817249).
- After switching the Diamond page to Demo, another check in the original conversation still returned Diamond and explained that a new chat was needed for Demo. The [Slack result](https://acquisityworkspace.slack.com/archives/C0BUF4GU8C8/p1789410718354279) agreed; the native source retained Diamond.
- "Can you pull up the result of that check again?" in Demo invoked `Get Foreman Result (Preview)` successfully at 18:33:27 UTC. Native Intercom events showed no new start, and no new Slack receipt appeared.
- A fresh Demo question, "Can you check which campaigns I have in this workspace?", received one acknowledgement and an automatic reply that campaign records were unavailable. It confirmed Demo/admin without inventing a list. The [Slack result](https://acquisityworkspace.slack.com/archives/C0BUF4GU8C8/p1789411044361819) matched. Earlier double acknowledgements prompted the Procedure wording fix above.
- The existing "I found a bug" quick message created conversation `215475935006975` with the correct Demo source URL. Its unchanged workflow immediately showed Jam recording/text options and teammate wait, without starting Foreman. The conversation is closed. Investigation routing and optional/late Jam behavior remain ENG-13767.

The actual Preview Slack connector `scl_ymNzljwUtw8fpGIPSumA` already had exactly one trigger to this branch at `/eve/v1/slack`; no retarget was needed. Branch-scoped `ACQUISITY_FIN_ORIGIN` was added and read back before deployment. Start direct triggering remains disabled and the Procedure audience remains Aaron-only Web.

Expiry, revoked access, impersonation, wrong app/contact/origin and result swaps have automated coverage; destructive session/membership changes were not all replayed live. Broader Slack, vision, cancellation and repository release UAT are not established by these Fin checks. This slice has no customer-record reads, so it cannot establish provider workspace isolation or diagnostic correctness. SDK credential lookup has the existing Connect cancellation exemption in `OUTSIDE-CALLS.md`; the bounded result-observation window starts after dispatch, not before the Slack receipt.

## Historical experiment evidence

The following observations belong to ENG-13759 and earlier runtime revisions. They are transport and presentation evidence, not current configuration or proof of ENG-13763 authorization.

- On 2026-09-12, the dedicated toolkit had 119 exact read approvals across existing providers, with a final default deny and no wildcard approvals. Provider grants still applied; Axiom authorization was expired at that check. This was an internal diagnostic experiment with a server-fixed workspace fixture, including Deep Lake Software Workspace for one approved case. That fixture is removed from the current identity flow.
- Commit `62b7b7f` passed three live synthetic connection tests with completed Eve runs and Slack receipts. Commit `9aa6dd2`, session `wrun_41M2BV5P2C0GYPFTXXRXQM0P82`, exercised production database, Autumn, Stripe and Instantly reads. A subsequent missing-handle request incorrectly started a synthetic probe, motivating fixed start/result actions. Those provider reads do not prove access to isolated Acquisity Preview data.
- Procedure run `wrun_41M2BYVSX40GX5DSWNH5X1XTQ5` proved callback delivery in about 80.6 seconds, but Fin misrepresented the report. After publishing real attribute chips, `wrun_41M2BZ4YF00GN0367V73HTSJ57` returned the report automatically in about 40.7 seconds. Foreman's own status interpretation and pagination claims were still wrong. A later names-only request, `wrun_41M2BZ9S6X0GPVY06AAB77N642`, returned automatically in about a minute; its internal handover still overstated campaign status.
- Presentation revision `72f9daf`, deployment `dpl_F9oEuTQe3vVcBPSqtbJSgirHu4qm`, passed validation, build and the 31-callback built GitHub proof. Conversation `215475916990248` returned campaign names automatically in 57 seconds and supported manual result retrieval without a new run. The fresh [conversation `215475917004291`](https://app.intercom.com/a/inbox/ls8uffkp/inbox/conversation/215475917004291) returned names after one acknowledgement in 31.8 seconds; its [Slack result](https://acquisityworkspace.slack.com/archives/C0BUF4GU8C8/p1789300124838459) matched. These runs establish the observed presentation only.
- Fin's built-in guard rejected an artificial marker request before any connector ran. Escalation guideline `352613` previously needed an Aaron-specific audience exception to permit the Procedure; verify that exception if escalation prevents a new test.

Long-run Slack completion was changed to update the original receipt from terminal channel events instead of the bounded HTTP observer. Runs started before that change lacked the saved receipt and were not repaired. This transport change did not add durable retries or prove customer authorization.
